arxiv-2102-13452.title: From integrability to chaos in quantum Liouvillians
arxiv-2102-13452.creator: Álvaro Rubio-García, Rafael A. Molina, Jorge Dukelsky
arxiv-2102-13452.description: Abstract The dynamics of open quantum systems can be described by a Liouvillian, which in the Markovian approximation fulfills the Lindblad master equation. We present a family of integrable many-body Liouvillians based on Richardson-Gaudin models with a complex structure of the jump operators.

arxiv-2108-03987.title: Learning Langevin dynamics with QCD phase transition
arxiv-2108-03987.creator: \firstname Lingxiao \lastname Wang, \firstname Lijia \lastname Jiang, \firstname Kai \lastname Zhou \fnsep
arxiv-2108-03987.description: Abstract In this proceeding, the deep Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs) are deployed to recognize the order of QCD phase transition and predict the dynamical parameters in Langevin processes. To overcome the intrinsic randomness existed in a stochastic process, we treat the final spectra as image-type inputs which preserve sufficient spatiotemporal correlations.

arxiv-2201-07332.title: Fragmentation in turbulence by small eddies
arxiv-2201-07332.creator: Yinghe Qi, Shiyong Tan, Noah Corbitt, Carl Urbanik, Ashwanth K. R. Salibindla, Rui Ni
arxiv-2201-07332.description: Abstract From air-sea gas exchange, oil pollution, to bioreactors, the ubiquitous fragmentation of bubbles/drops in turbulence has been modelled by relying on the classical Kolmogorov-Hinze paradigm since the 1950s. This framework hypothesizes that bubbles/drops are broken solely by eddies of the same size, even though turbulence is well known for its wide spectrum of scales.

arxiv-2202-13028.title: Healthsheet: Development of a Transparency Artifact for Health Datasets DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 111 8 CCS: Computer systems organization Embedded systems CCS: Computer systems organization Redundancy CCS: Computer systems organization Robotics CCS: Networks Network re
arxiv-2202-13028.creator: Negar Rostamzadeh, Diana Mincu, Subhrajit Roy, Andrew Smart, Lauren Wilcox, Mahima Pushkarna, Jessica Schrouff, Razvan Amironesei, Nyalleng Moorosi, Katherine Heller
arxiv-2202-13028.description: Abstract . Machine learning (ML) approaches have demonstrated promising results in a wide range of healthcare applications. Data plays a crucial role in developing ML-based healthcare systems that directly affect people’s lives. Many of the ethical issues surrounding the use of ML in healthcare stem from structural inequalities underlying the way we collect, use, and handle data.

arxiv-2210-04076.title: Robustness of Unsupervised Representation Learning without Labels
arxiv-2210-04076.creator: Aleksandar Petrov, Marta Kwiatkowska
arxiv-2210-04076.description: Abstract Unsupervised representation learning leverages large unlabeled datasets and is competitive with supervised learning. But non-robust encoders may affect downstream task robustness. Recently, robust representation encoders have become of interest. Still, all prior work evaluates robustness using a downstream classification task. Instead, we propose a family of unsupervised robustness measures, which are model- and task-agnostic and label-free.

arxiv-2212-02331.title: Proof of Renyi QNEC for free fermions
arxiv-2212-02331.creator: Pratik Roy
arxiv-2212-02331.description: Abstract Quantum null energy condition (QNEC) is usually stated as a bound on the expectation value of null components of the stress energy tensor at a point in terms of second null shape variations of the entanglement entropy at the same point.

arxiv-2304-05464.title: UnCRtainTS: Uncertainty Quantification for C loud R emoval in Optical Satellite T ime S eries
arxiv-2304-05464.creator: Patrick Ebel patrick.ebel@tum.de, Vivien Sainte Fare Garnot vsaint@ics.uzh.ch, Michael Schmitt michael.schmitt@unibw.de, Jan Dirk Wegner jandirk.wegner@uzh.ch, Xiao Xiang Zhu xiaoxiang.zhu@tum.de
arxiv-2304-05464.description: Abstract Clouds and haze often occlude optical satellite images, hindering continuous, dense monitoring of the Earth’s surface. Although modern deep learning methods can implicitly learn to ignore such occlusions, explicit cloud removal as pre-processing enables manual interpretation and allows training models when only few annotations are available.

arxiv-2402-03452.title: Entropy-Assisted Nanosecond Stochastic Operation in Perpendicular Superparamagnetic Tunnel Junctions
arxiv-2402-03452.creator: Lucile Soumah, Louise Desplat, Nhat-Tan Phan, Ahmed Sidi El Valli, Advait Madhavan, Florian Disdier, Stéphane Auffret, Ricardo C. Sousa,, Ursula Ebels,, Philippe Talatchian,
arxiv-2402-03452.description: Abstract We demonstrate a good agreement between mean dwell times measured in 50 nm diameter, perpendicularly magnetized superparamagnetic tunnel junctions (SMTJ), and theoretical predictions based on Langer’s theory. Due to a large entropic contribution, the theory yields Arrhenius prefactors in the femtosecond range for the measured junctions, in stark contrast to the typically assumed value of 1 ns.

arxiv-2404-12258.title: DeepLocalization: Using change point detection for Temporal Action Localization
arxiv-2404-12258.creator: Mohammed Shaiqur Rahman, Ibne Farabi Shihab, Lynna Chu, Anuj Sharma
arxiv-2404-12258.description: Abstract In this study, we introduce DeepLocalization, an innovative framework devised for the real-time localization of actions tailored explicitly for monitoring driver behavior. Utilizing the power of advanced deep learning methodologies, our objective is to tackle the critical issue of distracted driving—a significant factor contributing to road accidents.

arxiv-2505-12823.title: λ \lambda -matchability in cubic graphs
arxiv-2505-12823.creator: Santhosh Raghul, Nishad Kothari
arxiv-2505-12823.description: Abstract A vertex v v of a 2 2 -connected cubic graph G G is λ \lambda -matchable if G G has a spanning subgraph in which v v has degree three whereas every other vertex has degree one, and we let λ ⁡ ( G ) \lambda(G) denote the number of such vertices.

arxiv-2508-13047.title: Using AI for User Representation: An Analysis of 83 Persona Prompts
arxiv-2508-13047.creator: Joni Salminen, Danial Amin, Bernard J. Jansen
arxiv-2508-13047.description: Abstract We analyzed 83 persona prompts from 27 research articles that used large language models (LLMs) to generate user personas. Findings show that the prompts predominantly generate single personas. Several prompts express a desire for short or concise persona descriptions, which deviates from the tradition of creating rich, informative, and rounded persona profiles.

arxiv-2511-07084.title: Pandar128 dataset for lane line detection Thanks: The work has been supported by the grant of the University of West Bohemia, project No. SGS-2025-011. Computational resources were provided by the e-INFRA CZ project (ID:90254), supported by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Re
arxiv-2511-07084.creator: Filip Beránek, Václav Diviš, Ivan Gruber
arxiv-2511-07084.description: Abstract We present Pandar128, the largest public dataset for lane line detection using a 128-beam LiDAR. It contains over 52,000 camera frames and 34,000 LiDAR scans, captured in diverse real-world conditions in Germany. The dataset includes full sensor calibration (intrinsics, extrinsics) and synchronized odometry, supporting tasks such as projection, fusion, and temporal modeling.

arxiv-2511-21048.title: FedAPA: Federated Learning with Adaptive Prototype Aggregation Toward Heterogeneous Wi-Fi CSI-based Crowd Counting Thanks: Thanks:
arxiv-2511-21048.creator: Jingtao Guo, Yuyi Mao
arxiv-2511-21048.description: Abstract Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI)-based sensing provides a non-invasive, device-free approach for tasks such as human activity recognition and crowd counting, but large-scale deployment is hindered by the need for extensive site-specific training data. Federated learning (FL) offers a way to avoid raw data sharing but is challenged by heterogeneous sensing data and device resources.

arxiv-2511-22540.title: Anomalous double-layer restructuring in water-in-salt electrolytes at graphitic interfaces governs capacitance
arxiv-2511-22540.creator: Hannah O. Wood, Fulu Zhou, Jan Dočkal, Martin Lísal, Filip Moučka, Sittipong Kaewmorakot, Robert A. W. Dryfe, Paola Carbone
arxiv-2511-22540.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hannah O. Wood, Fulu Zhou, Jan Dočkal, Martin Lísal, Filip Moučka, Sittipong Kaewmorakot, Robert A. W. Dryfe, Paola Carbone. The structure and thickness of the electrical double layer (EDL) at carbon electrodes strongly influence electrochemical performance, yet remain poorly understood in super-concentrated aqueous electrolytes.

arxiv-2602-04352.title: Mosaic Learning: A Framework for Decentralized Learning with Model Fragmentation
arxiv-2602-04352.creator: Sayan Biswas, Davide Frey, Romaric Gaudel, Nirupam Gupta, Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Dimitri Lerévérend, Rafael Pires, Rishi Sharma, François Taïani, Martijn de Vos
arxiv-2602-04352.description: Abstract DL ( DL ) enables collaborative ML ( ML ) without a central server, making it suitable for settings where training data cannot be centrally hosted. We introduce Mosaic Learning, a DL framework that decomposes models into fragments and disseminates them independently across the network.

arxiv-2602-13503.title: Hermes: Large DEL Datasets Train Generalizable Protein-Ligand Binding Prediction Models
arxiv-2602-13503.creator: Maxwell Kleinsasser, Brayden J. Halverson, Edward Kraft, Sean Francis-Lyon, Sarah E. Hugo, Mackenzie R. Roman, Ben Miller, Andrew D. Blevins, Ian K. Quigley
arxiv-2602-13503.description: Abstract The quality and consistency of training data remain critical bottlenecks for protein-ligand binding prediction. Public affinity datasets, aggregated from thousands of labs and assay formats, introduce biases that limit model generalization and complicate evaluation. DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DELs) offer a potential solution: unified experimental protocols generating massive binding datasets across diverse chemical and protein target space.

arxiv-2602-18425.title: RVR: Retrieve-Verify-Retrieve for Comprehensive Question Answering
arxiv-2602-18425.creator: Deniz Qian, Hung-Ting Chen, Eunsol Choi
arxiv-2602-18425.description: Abstract Comprehensively retrieving diverse documents is crucial to address queries that admit a wide range of valid answers. We introduce retrieve-verify-retrieve (RVR), a multi-round retrieval framework designed to maximize answer coverage. Initially, a retriever takes the original query and returns a candidate document set, followed by a verifier that identifies a high-quality subset.

europmc-pmc9226045.creator: Lopez-Leon S, Wegman-Ostrosky T, Ayuzo Del Valle NC, Perelman C, Sepulveda R, Rebolledo PA, Cuapio A, Villapol S.

We have used PubMed and Embase to identify observational studies published

pmc-10603324.title: Relationship between retinal microvascular impairment and subclinical atherosclerosis in SLE
pmc-10603324.creator: Sara Ferrigno, Paola Conigliaro, Stefano Rizza, Susanna Longo, Carolina Nesi, Federico Carlucci, Alberto Bergamini, Raffaele Mancino, Carlo Nucci, Massimo Federici, Maria Sole Chimenti, Massimo Cesareo
pmc-10603324.description: ObjectivesPatients with SLE have higher cardiovascular (CV) risk compared with healthy controls (HC) and are characterised by accelerated atherosclerosis; intima media thickness (IMT), marker of subclinical atherosclerosis, is higher in patients with SLE than in HCs. Retinal microvascular impairment detected through optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) was investigated as a marker of systemic vascular involvement in SLE.

pmc-11425983.title: Myxomatous Mysteries: Decoding the Oral Focal Mucinosis
pmc-11425983.creator: Saptarshi Das, Arunit Chatterjee, Rudra Prasad Chatterjee, Sangeeta Sinha, Mehebuba Sultana, Sk Abdul Mahmud, Neha Shah, Mousumi Pal
pmc-11425983.description: Oral focal mucinosis (OFM) is a unique benign lesion of the oral cavity with uncertain etiology which is analogous to cutaneous focal mucinosis. It mainly affects women in their fourth and fifth decades of life. The diagnosis of this condition is based on histopathological examination, as it lacks characteristic clinical and radiographic features.

pmc-12517713.title: The carbon footprint of modern imaging
pmc-12517713.creator: Jan Vosshenrich, Elmar M Merkle, Tobias Heye
pmc-12517713.description: Purpose of reviewThis review aims to highlight the often-overlooked environmental impact of medical imaging in urological practice, focusing on energy consumption, associated carbon emissions, and practical strategies for reducing the carbon footprint of imaging modalities.Recent findingsMedical imaging accounts for a significant proportion of a hospital's total energy use, with MRI, CT, and PET-CT being the most energy-intensive modalities.

pmc-12617666.title: Contrast negation increases face pareidolia rates in natural scenes
pmc-12617666.creator: Benjamin Balas, Myra Morton, Molly Setchfield, Lily Roshau, Emily Westrick
pmc-12617666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Face pareidolia, the phenomenon of seeing face-like patterns in non-face images, has a dual nature: Pareidolic patterns are experienced as face-like, even while observers can recognize the true nature of the stimulus (Stuart et al., 2025). Although pareidolic faces seem to result largely from the canonical arrangement of eye spots and a mouth, we hypothesized that competition between veridical and face-like interpretations of pareidolic patterns may constrain face pareidolia in natural scenes and textures.

pmc-12790703.title: Mitral Papillary Fibroelastoma Revealed by Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
pmc-12790703.creator: Zineb Rahali, Badre El Boussaadani, Zainab Raissouni
pmc-12790703.description: Papillary fibroelastoma (PFE) is a very rare benign primary cardiac tumor that preferentially affects heart valves and may lead to severe embolic events. Its diagnosis is now easily suggested by echocardiography, and surgical excision is a safe and effective treatment to prevent recurrence.

pmc-12836830.title: Homocysteine levels alter the TyG index-CKD link in Chinese hypertensive patients
pmc-12836830.creator: Wei Zhou, Chao Yu, Huihui Bao, Xiaoshu Cheng
pmc-12836830.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and aimsHomocysteine (Hcy) is an established non-traditional risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and CKD, and how this association may be modified by Hcy levels, remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether the association between the TyG index and CKD in hypertensive patients is modified by Hcy levels and to examine this potential interaction.Methods and results26679 subjects were included in this multicenter observational study.

pmc-13072888.title: Functional Characterization of Solanum tuberosum ER Lumen Binding Protein (StBiP) Genes Through Complementation in Yeast kar2 Deletion Mutants
pmc-13072888.creator: Binita Adhikari, Donna M. Gordon, Jeanmarie Verchot
pmc-13072888.description: Yeast models are widely used to study molecular chaperones from diverse organisms, including plants, because of their well-characterized genetics and the conservation of the protein-folding machinery among eukaryotes. Cross-species complementation studies in yeast have yielded valuable insights into conserved biochemical activity and molecular functions that manage protein folding, assembly, and repair during stress.

pmc-13143713.title: Gas dissection from the thorax to the abdomen
pmc-13143713.creator: Marina Manica Tamiozzo, Letícia Dalmolin, Mariana Manica Tamiozzo
pmc-13143713.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A chest tube was placed. An initial suspicion of hollow viscus perforation was ruled out after exploratory laparotomy showed no visceral injury. The combination of imaging findings and clinical context strongly suggested barotrauma secondary to excessive positive-pressure ventilation. This likely resulted in alveolar rupture due to elevated intrathoracic pressure, with air dissecting along bronchovascular sheaths-a phenomenon known as the Macklin effect.

pmc-13217858.title: A city-scale optimization framework for biomass-to-clean-energy transitions: The KAMPALA-TIMES model
pmc-13217858.creator: Ismail Kimuli, John Baptist Kirabira, Francis Mujjuni
pmc-13217858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryRapid urbanization in Sub-Saharan African cities is accompanied by persistent reliance on traditional biomass for household energy, posing challenges for climate mitigation, public health, and sustainable development. This study develops the KAMPALA-TIMES model, a city-scale, bottom-up optimization framework that integrates localized energy data with IPCC AR6 SSP-RCP pathways to evaluate long-term energy transition strategies for Kampala, Uganda, from 2022 to 2060. Four scenarios (business-as-usual, enhanced biomass utilization, mixed renewable integration, and policy-driven carbon reduction) are assessed.

pmc-13618248.title: Photophysics of Doubly Reduced Quinacridone Dyes: Toward Redox Reactivity Activated by Red Light
pmc-13618248.creator: Elena Rossin, Björn Pfund, Martina Chirico, Tobia Casadei, Giacomo Morselli, Catia Nicoletti, Mathis Brändlin, Sara Bonacchi, Marco Fantin, Pierluca Galloni, Oliver S. Wenger, Andrea Sartorel
pmc-13618248.description: Super-reductive photocatalysis is an emerging approach to broaden the conventional organic reactivity by exploiting reduced forms of a parent photocatalyst (PC) as the actual photoactive super-reductant. Recent reports have highlighted the advantages of using closed-shell, doubly reduced PC2– with respect to open-shell, singly reduced PC•–, with the former having longer excited-state lifetime and enlarged reductive power.
